brief: Academy's Tchir attributes this week's price action to supply constraints (bonds, energy, chips), stop-losses across markets, and false liquidity rather than the week's political headlines (a Russia/Iran sanctions waiver, Starlink/Ukraine reliability reports, a Greenland oil post markets shrugged off). On yields, the 10-year's three-month climb from 4.4% to 5.35% reversed into a 17bp drop this week, which he attributes to fading expectations for compute-related debt issuance, not economic data, the Fed, or the deficit. On credit, he raises his alert from yellow to orange, pointing to a 50bp German versus French and Italian 2-year blowout, dealers pulling back in two-week-old new issues, and compute-linked spread widening, and expects the currently orderly move to turn disorderly, with downside risk (10-20bp IG, 3-5pt HY) outweighing a move tighter. He extends the same positioning and false-liquidity risk to equities, flagging heavy leveraged-ETF exposure in the top-heavy Nasdaq 100 and SOXX, and stays cautious because the stress sits in compute names driving index returns. He remains long energy producers, expecting diesel relief to be smaller than headlined and any Middle East or Russia-Ukraine resolution to trigger only a brief sell-off.
